entry.label: What the boundary cannot carry alone
entry.description: A relational encounter can improve while the organisation behind it remains unchanged. Taylor and Boxer distinguish form of response, scope of holding, health and fit, then propose four organisational conditions for sustaining relational public services.

profile.why_it_matters: It makes the organisational demands behind relational practice explicit, including what evidence must be able to change.
key_distinctions: Form of response differs from scope of holding.
A wider scope is not necessarily healthier or better fitted to demand.
Relational behaviour differs from authority to revise rules and resources.
practice_connections: Start with actual demand in citizens’ words.
Ask who carries the work and risk, and what happens to learning.
open_checks: The authors describe a practitioner proposition, not a validated instrument.
